description: We are AstroSharks, a passionate high school team, excited about space exploration, robotics, coding, AI, and solving real-world problems through technology. We bring creativity, teamwork, and innovative thinking to the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary: Our project is a 2D pixel-art survival adventure game developed using the Godot Engine and accessible through a web browser. Designed for children, teenagers, and adults, the game allows players to experience the challenges astronauts face while exploring Mars. Throughout their journey, players must complete missions, manage essential resources, overcome environmental hazards, and make critical decisions to survive. By combining interactive gameplay with real scientific concepts, players can learn about space exploration while having fun. Our project is important because it makes space education more accessible, engaging, and exciting, encouraging curiosity, critical thinking, and inspiring future generations to explore the possibilities of space.
details:
Cóndor Rojo is a browser-based, 2D pixel-art survival adventure developed using the Godot Engine. Designed primarily for children ages 7–12, but accessible to older players, the game puts players in the role of an Ecuadorian astronaut on a ten-sol mission to explore and survive on Mars, assisted by INTI, a robotic companion.

Players begin by choosing an equipment kit with different strengths and limitations. As they explore, they must manage oxygen, energy, and food while maintaining their outpost, repairing solar panels, growing crops, and completing scientific missions. These include recovering data from historic Mars rovers, collecting mineral samples, searching for water ice, and investigating Jezero Crater and Martian caves. Dust storms, solar radiation, and delayed communication with Earth introduce additional challenges. Decisions have consequences: seeking shelter offers protection but consumes supplies, while longer expeditions demand careful resource planning.

Unlike a conventional educational presentation, Cóndor Rojo lets players learn through the consequences of their decisions. Its science draws on archived NASA data and research, including DONKI space-weather records, JPL Horizons communication delays, OSDR and RadLab studies, and Mars Trek geographic information. Scientific facts and source references appear within the game, while simulated gameplay values are distinguished from real measurements.

We developed the game with Godot, GDScript, Visual Studio Code, Python, Art App, and GitHub, alongside HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the website. Feedback and playtesting have helped us refine the experience to make it approachable, entertaining, and educational.

Our goal is to show younger audiences how astronauts balance competing risks and resources, inspiring curiosity about Mars, science, and future space missions.
